references.text: The introduction to the offerings of the Feast of Tabernacles, which provides context for the daily sacrifices described from verse 12 onward.
The first day of the Feast of Tabernacles with 13 bulls, illustrating the pattern where the number of bulls decreases by one each day. Day two has 12 bulls.
Grain offerings and drink offerings associated with the animals mentioned in verse 17, completing the instructions for the second day.
Previous instructions that the sacrificial animals must be without blemish (תְּמִימִם), the same requirement stated in verse 17.
Basic instructions about the Feast of Tabernacles in Leviticus, which Numbers 29 expands upon with specific sacrifice instructions.
The daily burnt offering that forms the foundation for the additional festival offerings described in Numbers 29.
Ezra mentions the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles with the prescribed daily burnt offerings, in accordance with the instructions in Numbers 29.
